issues.failure_explanation: When S_free is empty every variable in Iup sits at a bound that the KKT table forces to satisfy tau_i <= -rho (alpha_k=0 gives tau_k <= -rho; alpha_k^*=C_k gives tau_{N+k} <= -rho), and every variable in Idown satisfies tau_j >= -rho. Hence the correct chain is max_{Iup} tau_i <= -rho <= min_{Idown} tau_j, i.e. tau_{i*} <= -rho <= tau_{j*}. The source reverses both inequalities, stating tau_{i*} >= -rho >= tau_{j*}, which contradicts the table in the same paper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both \geq in eq:bias-bounds with \leq so the chain reads max_{Iup} tau_i = tau_{i*} <= -rho <= min_{Idown} tau_j = tau_{j*}.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed bound on -rho in the no-free-support-vector degenerate case is stated with the wrong direction. The midpoint bias formula (eq:bias-midpoint) and the algorithm's fallback step are unaffected because they do not rely on the inequality direction, but a reader using the stated bounds to reason about the location of the true bias relative to tau_{i*} and tau_{j*} would draw the wrong conclusion.
issues.title: Reversed inequality direction in degenerate bias bounds
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local two-symbol correction (flip both inequality signs) fully determined by the KKT table already in the source. No downstream theorem, algorithm step, or guarantee changes; the midpoint heuristic and the SMO loop are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark asserts that the degenerate case eta <= 0 is impossible for the RBF kernel when all training points are distinct. However, the working-set selection (eq:mvp) does not forbid i* = k and j* = N+k for the same training point k, which requires only alpha_k < C_k (so k in Iup) and alpha_k^* < C_k (so N+k in Idown) — two independent conditions. When p = q = k, the curvature formula gives eta = Omega_{kk} - 2 Omega_{kk} + Omega_{kk} = 0 for any positive kernel, including RBF. Thus eta = 0 is achievable with all x_k pairwise distinct, contradicting the remark's claim.

failure_location.quote:
This case cannot arise for the RBF kernel (m1) with distinct
training points but may occur for m2 with $a = -1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sentence with a correct statement: for the RBF kernel with distinct training points eta >= 0 always, and eta = 0 can occur when the selected pair corresponds to the same training point (p = q); the fallback in this remark handles that case as well as the eta < 0 case possible for m2 with a = -1.
issues.overall_effect: The remark provides an incorrect guarantee about the RBF case, potentially leading a reader to omit the eta <= 0 fallback check for m1. The algorithm itself (line 12 of Algorithm alg:smo) does include the check, so the implementation is safe, but the stated theoretical exclusion is false.
issues.title: False claim that eta <= 0 cannot arise for RBF with distinct training points
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local rewrite of one sentence in a remark. The algorithm already includes the eta <= 0 branch, so no procedure, guarantee, or downstream result changes. The mathematical error is a false exclusion claim, not a broken inference or construction.
